chapter: After Basie: Cafe Society to Los Angeles
title: Card games in Los Angeles and the night of the raid
summary: Women in Los Angeles played blackjack, tonk and bingo-like games constantly. At a game she co-hosted with a singer named Helen on 43rd Street, the police under Mayor Bradley raided it; they paid $5 and resumed for two days.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah. You know when I first came out here everybody used to - all the women, they didn't do nothing but play cards, you know. They used to have

big blackjack games and tonk games and sometimes they used to have like little bingo games. It wasn't bingo games; they used to call it something else; but anyway the first time I ever worked it was in a raid. The Mayor raided.

And there was a girl singer here. Her name was Helen. What was Helen's last name? Anyway, she was a big, heavyset girl and she sang good. And she had an apartment over there, on 43rd Street. And she said, "Helen, come on and have a game with me, cause they come to your games cause they think you have a lot of money and they come to you". And I said, "well, I'll have a game with you". So we was having this game and it was crowded. We had tables in all the rooms and everything. We had a big crowd. After awhile we heard a knock on the door and here comes Scotty and Mayor Bradley. And there was two boys sitting at the table and they wasn't playing, and I said, 'honey get up and give these gentlemen a seat'. Scotty said, "sent for you

yesterday and here you comes today". They said, "Helen that's a raid". I said, "raid, what's that"? And then he said, you all have to come down town with us. And they took us down there and they booked us. And we paid $5, and come on back and had a game for two days. I didn't know about raids and all that stuff.
So little old private games they raid? And you pay just a little fine?
Yeah. I guess they just had nothing else to do.
Somebody had tipped them off or something?
